entries.title: keep package modules in the program's own golden
entries.body:
tests/self/goldens.js split a program's checker dump only on plain and
entry module headers, so a `module … [package …]` block was glued onto
whichever module was dumped before it, and a src/ module imported after
nish/ package modules dumped differently under two programs. A package
header now closes the current module, and the package's lines are kept in
the program's own golden under its entry line, compared per program: package
modules carry each program's instantiations, so they cannot be deduplicated.
The regenerated goldens are a pure reorder; the sorted lines are identical.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: install the main package with its pins stamped, as release.yml publishes it
entries.body:
The package section packed the checkout as it stands and installed that. Since #1039 the release commit moves only `version`, and the platform pins follow in release.yml's lockfile pull request, so between the two `main` is nish@0.27.0 pinning @amritk/nish-x86_64-linux@0.26.0. The staged platform package (0.27.0) did not satisfy that pin, npm fetched the published 0.26.0 and nested it under nish/node_modules/, and the launcher ran it: seven checks failed, CI on main went red at the 0.27.0 release commit, and the release's own CI gate held back the publish.

The section now unpacks the tarball, pins it to its own version with scripts/pin-platform-packages.mjs exactly as the release job does before `npm pack`, and packs it again, so `files` still decides what ships and the checkout is never edited. A new check asserts nothing is nested under the installed main package, which names this regression directly instead of through its seven symptoms.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon
